scores.evidence: check proposed actions against a deterministic policy layer *outside* the LLM. Running in the sandbox limits the damage even if the agent is manipulated.
scores.rationale: Mostly correct (App, delivery-ID idempotency, fail-on-base check), with minor imprecision such as delimiters as injection defense, but nothing design-breaking.

scores.evidence: Mark the issue `agent-eligible` only if all of these hold: it is a bug or docs issue with clear reproduction steps
scores.rationale: Covers triage and resolution with sensible eligibility gating, explicit non-goals and buildable phasing; retrieval and claim/yield details are thin.

scores.evidence: an explicit state machine for each issue: `NEW → TRIAGED → (NEEDS_INFO | ROUTED_HUMAN | ELIGIBLE) → REPRODUCING → FIXING → VERIFYING → PR_OPEN → DONE/ABANDONED`
scores.rationale: Consistent design with clear stage responsibilities and a permissions matrix; only minor loose ends.

scores.evidence: replay historical issues against the commit just before the real fix... Run this on every prompt or model change.
scores.rationale: Offline benchmark, shadow mode, phase gates and online metrics target the main risks, but thresholds are asserted without justification and per-action precision thresholds are not defined.

scores.evidence: Pick 1–2 pilot repos with good test coverage and willing maintainers.
scores.rationale: Some assumptions implicit, and numbers like ~200 LOC, 90%, 50% are given without labeling as provisional or sensitivity analysis.

scores.evidence: Flaky tests misleading the agent: rerun failures, keep a known-flaky test list, and require the reproduction to fail deterministically.
scores.rationale: Covers injection, spam, flaky tests, wrong fixes, security disclosure, circuit breaker and escalation, but bot loops, mid-work edits and partial-failure recovery are thin.

scores.evidence: Dashboard: shows the issue pipeline, costs, acceptance rates, and items waiting on humans.
scores.rationale: Dashboard, kill switch, audit log and rollout gates exist, but deployment, rollback, incident ownership, alerting and index migration are missing.

scores.evidence: set token, time, and compute caps per issue, per day, and per repo... cheaper models first for triage
scores.rationale: Budgets and model tiering are identified but with '$X' placeholders, no cost estimate or scaling analysis, and multi-candidate fix cost goes unremarked.

scores.evidence: Each phase needs its metric thresholds met and maintainer sign-off before the next one starts.
scores.rationale: Phase gating and a human merge gate limit irreversibility, but there is no discussion of vendor, model or embedding lock-in, or data model and audit format choices.

scores.evidence: narrow agents, one per stage, each with its own prompt and its own tool allowlist. This is safer and easier to evaluate
scores.rationale: Mostly proportionate with staged rollout; multi-candidate generation and four agents plus a vector index are somewhat heavy but justified.

scores.evidence: Build the offline replay benchmark from about 200 historical issues.
scores.rationale: Ordered phases with durations and concrete stage steps, but technology choices (queue, store, index) and exit-criteria numbers are left open.

checklist.evidence: The GitHub App gets least-privilege scopes, and branch protection requires human approval.
check proposed actions against a deterministic policy layer *outside* the LLM.
Network access is limited to package registries, and there are no production credentials.
Confirm the new test fails on the base branch and passes with the fix.
Compare the agent's labels with the actual labels... Run this on every prompt or model change.
Log every outcome: merged, edited then merged, closed, or reverted.
a repo-level config flag and a `/agent stop` command pause the agent immediately.
set token, time, and compute caps per issue, per day, and per repo.
Every action is written to an append-only audit log.
embeddings of the codebase... refreshed on each push to the default branch.
Events are idempotent and keyed by delivery ID.

traps.evidence: Secrets never enter the sandbox or the LLM context.
treat issue text, comments, and repository content as untrusted data.
PR acceptance rate of 50% or more for agent-authored PRs. Track the revert rate too.
capped by a budget, for example 8 iterations, 30 minutes, and $X of tokens.

note: Solid, well-gated design with strong safety posture and a human merge gate; weaker on operations, cost grounding, retrieval/index specifics and assumption labeling.
